A London street corner scene. At the centre, a handsome six-storey corner office building standing at a Y-junction where two streets diverge: warm sand-coloured brick upper floors with pale stone banding between them, regular rectangular windows in even rows, a chamfered corner facing the viewer, a stone-clad ground floor with tall dark shopfront glazing, and a set-back top floor with dormer windows. To the left, a taller pale stone mansion block recedes down the left street. To the right, a row of lower older shopfronts with a painted timber frontage. Street furniture drawn plainly: two tall lamp posts, a slim vertical banner on a pole, traffic lights, road markings and a zebra crossing. A red double-decker bus crosses the near left foreground, and a cyclist rides the empty road at centre with a few small pedestrian figures on the pavements, all seen at a distance from behind or in silhouette. Flat pale overcast sky above.

Ligne claire clear-line comic album illustration. One even unvarying black outline of consistent weight on every single shape. Flat unmodulated colour fills. Absolutely no gradients, no cast shadows, no shading, no hatching, no texture, no photorealism, no 3D rendering. Strict palette only: pale sky blue, paper white, sand ochre, album yellow, sea green, steel blue, and one adventure red reserved for the bus alone. IMPORTANT: no text, no lettering, no words, no numbers, no logos, no brand marks, no shop signage, no watermarks anywhere in the image.
